contract_plain_english: In the mean-zero sub-exponential setting of Theorem 2.8.1, choose a real λ whose magnitude is at most an unspecified positive absolute constant c divided by the largest psi-one norm among X_1,...,X_N. Then property e of Proposition 2.7.1, together with absolute-constant equivalence of its parameter and the psi-one norm, gives for every i the bound E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²), where C is another positive absolute constant. Equation (2.24) and this immediately following MGF-use sentence appear on PDF page 25/printed page 36.

source_evidence.observation: To bound each MGF, the proof invokes property e of Proposition 2.7.1 and says λ must be small enough.

The displayed sufficient restriction is |λ| ≤ c / max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1}, with a non-strict inequality, absolute value on λ, a lower-case absolute constant c in the numerator, and the maximum psi-one norm in the denominator.
Under the restriction, the proof states that E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ^2 ||X_i||_{psi_1}^2) for each term X_i.
For a mean-zero X, property e is E exp(λX) ≤ exp(K_5^2 λ^2) for all |λ| ≤ 1/K_5. Proposition 2.7.1 says its parameters differ by at most an absolute constant factor.

The source explains that property e holds for a K_5 within an absolute constant factor of ||X||_{psi_1}; this is the reason unspecified absolute constants c and C appear in the uniform restriction and MGF bound.
The sub-exponential norm is ||X||_{psi_1} = inf{s > 0 : E exp(|X|/s) ≤ 2}.

binders: N is the implicitly positive number of variables (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
X_1,...,X_N are real random variables in the inherited Theorem 2.8.1 setting (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
λ is a real MGF parameter, allowed to have either sign because Equation (2.24) constrains |λ| (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).

c and C denote positive absolute constants, independent of N, the X_i, i, and λ; their numerical values are unspecified (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24), following sentence, and footnote 8).
conclusions: For every i = 1,...,N, E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence immediately following Equation (2.24)).
definitions_and_conventions: ||X||_{psi_1} = inf{s > 0 : E exp(|X|/s) ≤ 2} (PDF page 22/printed page 33, Definition 2.7.5 and Equation (2.21)).
max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1} is the maximum individual sub-exponential norm over i = 1,...,N (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
Property e states that a mean-zero sub-exponential variable has a quadratic MGF bound for |λ| at most the reciprocal of an appropriate parameter K_5 (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1).
Footnote 8 permits replacement of K_5 by ||X_i||_{psi_1} at the cost of unspecified absolute constants c and C (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
hypotheses: Each X_i is mean zero and sub-exponential (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1; PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1 property e).
The enclosing theorem assumes the X_i are jointly independent, although independence is not needed for the individual MGF estimate itself (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Theorem 2.8.1).
implicit_context: Equation (2.24) is a sufficient uniform restriction ensuring property e can be applied simultaneously to every X_i (PDF page 25/printed page 36, paragraph surrounding Equation (2.24)).
The use of the maximum norm makes the same λ valid for all indices, even when the X_i have different norms (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24) and following sentence).
Mean zero is essential for property e as stated; Proposition 2.7.1 adds property e only under the additional assumption E X = 0 (PDF page 21/printed page 32).
The MGF bounds are intended for substitution into the product in Equation (2.23) (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following the individual MGF estimate).

details: The restriction is two-sided in λ because it uses |λ|, and equality at the boundary is permitted (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
The denominator is the maximum psi-one norm, not a sum, average, or norm of the vector of norms (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).

The numerator c and exponent coefficient C are unspecified positive absolute constants arising from equivalence of sub-exponential parameters (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24), following sentence, and footnote 8).
Neither c nor C may depend on N, i, the distribution of X_i, or λ (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1 absolute-constant-factor statement; PDF page 25/printed page 36, footnote 8).
The exponent is quadratic in λ and in ||X_i||_{psi_1}: C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}² (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).
The conclusion is an individual bound for each i, not yet a product or summed exponent (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).

undebatable_constraints: Equation (2.24) is |λ| ≤ c / max_i ||X_i||_{psi_1}, with absolute value on λ and a non-strict inequality (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The denominator is exactly the maximum individual psi-one norm (PDF page 25/printed page 36, Equation (2.24)).
The immediately following conclusion is E exp(λX_i) ≤ exp(C λ² ||X_i||_{psi_1}²) for each i (PDF page 25/printed page 36).
The exponent contains λ² and the square of the individual norm, not the maximum norm (PDF page 25/printed page 36, sentence following Equation (2.24)).
The constants c and C are positive absolute constants with unspecified numerical values (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1; PDF page 25/printed page 36, footnote 8).
Mean zero is required for the invoked property e (PDF page 21/printed page 32, Proposition 2.7.1).
Equation (2.24) is a sufficient simultaneous small-λ condition, not an equivalence or a necessary condition (PDF page 25/printed page 36, wording 'if λ is small enough so that').
